thread:
maya: Heads up - noticed a sharp drop in prefix cache hit rate for prod v2 over the last ~2hrs. From ~72% -> ~18%. I think it lines up with the 3f2a7d deploy. Anyone else seeing this?

liam: looking now. can you post the hit-rate by tenant? any obvious outsized ones?

sana: quick numbers: overall hit-rate by tenant (top 5 by qps):
- tenant-a: 81% -> 19%
- tenant-b: 69% -> 17%
- tenant-c: 74% -> 20%
- tenant-d: 60% -> 15%
- tenant-e: 77% -> 18%

sana: checked the deploy diff for 3f2a7d - there was a small refactor in cache key building in runtime/cache/keying.go. Old key: 

```
// prior
key := sha256(tenantID + ":" + modelName + ":" + prefixHash)
```

sana: new key dropped tenantID accidentally: 

```
// introduced in 3f2a7d
key := sha256(modelName + ":" + prefixHash)
```

sana: that explains collisions across tenants and the sudden drop in per-tenant hit rate (lots of churn and evictions).

rob (sec-eng): this is a serious privacy/iso issue - if entries are shared between tenants we need to treat this as a potential data exposure. Even if contents are non-PII, we must assume worst-case.

rob (sec-eng): immediate asks: 1) roll back the keying change in prod 2) run an audit to list keys that may have been created while keying was tenantless 3) snapshot affected cache nodes for forensics

infra-bot: rollback job queued for service=runtime-cache pool=prod-v2 user=liam

liam: rolling back now. patch PR: https://git.redwood/infra/runtime/pull/432

maya: thank you. while rolling back, is there any chance entries that got shared are still being served across tenants (i.e., server nodes still have the wrong keys)? we need a mitigation not just rollback.

sana: good point. even after rollback older entries (built without tenantID) will remain until evicted. options:
- proactively delete any entries whose key format matches the tenantless pattern (scan keys)
- add a runtime filter: if entry found check entry.metadata.tenant != request.tenant => deny
- encrypt cache values with tenant-bound nonce so even if key collision happens the value is tenant-locked

liam: scan + delete seems fastest. but scanning Redis clusters of sharded prefix-cache is heavy. we could add a short-circuit check in Get: when we compute key we also check a stored metadata header that contains tenantID and reject if mismatch. That requires storing tenantID in value metadata for all entries (small overhead).

rob (sec-eng): metadata option is safer and auditable. We should also emit an audit log event whenever a tenant mismatch occurs (include key hash, node, timestamp, request/entry tenant ids).

sana: implementing metadata check now. patch includes: store JSON header with fields {tenant, model, created_at, key_format_version} and encrypt value with optional tenant envelope if enabled.

sana: code snippet:
```
entry = GetRaw(key)
meta = parseHeader(entry)
if meta.tenant != req.tenant { emit_audit("cache_tenant_mismatch", {key, meta.tenant, req.tenant}) ; return MISS }
return deserialize(entry.value)
```

maya: perf tradeoff? extra parse on hit path adds latency. any numbers?

sana: local microbench: header parse adds ~0.4ms median to Get path for small values; envelope decrypt (if enabled) adds ~1.8ms + CPU. On high QPS hot paths that is material. But we can gate with feature flag: enable metadata-only check (no encrypt) cluster-wide quickly, and enable envelope encryption later for high-security tenants.

liam: for warmup: we lost a lot of cached prefixes. we should rehydrate top prefixes per-tenant via backfill job rather than try to rely on natural traffic. propose a k=500 top prefixes job run per-tenant distributed in background with rate limit.

sana: agreed. backfill job will use kv-analytics to pick top-K prefixes by recent freq and do a Fetch+Put to repopulate. we'll ensure backfill writes headers with correct tenant.

rob (sec-eng): audit concerns: we need to produce a report of potential cross-tenant hits during the window [1751994000..1752001200] - include list of request IDs, keys, affected tenants, and whether any value looked like PII (heuristic). This is timeboxed.

maya: creating an incident ticket and assigning to sec+infra+runtime. short-term action items in thread:
1) liam: rollback 3f2a7d (in progress) - due: asap
2) sana: deploy metadata-check patch to prod as hotfix w/ feature flag - due: 30m
3) infra: schedule Redis key-scan job to list suspicious keys for forensics - due: 1hr
4) ops: run backfill/top-K prefix repop job after metadata-check deployed - due: 2hr
5) rob/sec: produce cross-tenant exposure report - due: 4hr

liam: rollback done. canaries look good for 10m. starting rollout to rest of cluster.

infra-bot: rollback complete. job=rollback-3f2a7d status=success duration=12m

sana: metadata-check patch submitted and canary deployed to 2 nodes. no mismatches observed in canary logs so far. audit events are being emitted to seq.

maya: careful re: perf - enable metadata-only check cluster-wide but hold encryption toggle. we can schedule a perf-optimized envelope later (e.g., use AES-GCM with cached tenant keys in memory and avoid KMS per-request).

rob (sec-eng): agree. also require storing audit logs in an append-only backed store and enable retention policy for 90 days for these events.

sana: added unit tests and a fuzz test that ensures cache keys unique across tenant permutations. added CI guard to prevent keying drops like this from merging again.

maya: thanks everyone. follow-ups: postmortem and checklist for cache key changes (code review tag + security signoff). I'll open the postmortem and assign authors.

- maya
